candidate.answerReason: There are four first-draw possibilities. Each allows four second-draw possibilities with replacement and three without replacement.

methods.label: Count second-draw choices for each first draw
methods.explanation: With replacement, each draw has 4 possible outcomes, giving \(4\times4=16\) outcomes in total. Without replacement, only 3 possibilities remain for the second draw, giving \(4\times3=12\) outcomes in total.
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary ordered pair counting and the Grade 9 distinction between replacement and nonreplacement.
